transcript: If you need to know the plan, read every message twice and can't relax unless everything is in order. This didn't start in adulthood. It started the first time your home felt like a place you had to survive. You never knew which version of your parents would appear. Warm one moment. Angry the next. Present one day, absent the following. Your nervous system learned early. Uncertainty is danger. So you adapted. You learned to anticipate, to manage, to stay two steps ahead. If you could control the environment, maybe you could avoid the pain. You became independent too soon, responsible before it was fair. Strong in ways children should never have to be. For some, the chaos went deeper. Boundaries were broken. Safety was taken. Control became the only form of protection. And now, in adulthood, your body still remembers. You analyze messages. You sense subtle shifts. You struggle to relax into trust. Not because you are difficult, but because your nervous system is still living in a world that once felt unsafe. That control is not ego. It is a frightened inner child trying to survive. And healing does not begin by managing everyone else. It begins when you turn inward and meet the little girl who learned control instead of safety. You are not too much. You are still waiting to feel safe. This is not about fixing yourself. It is about meeting the part of you that learned to survive. The 30-day healing journey is there for that process. You can find it in my profile.
